_help: Per commodity, an indicator->1-5 map (5 = bullish). A bare number or {"score": n, "note": "why"} for auditability. Unset = held at neutral and excluded from the average, exactly like fundamentals_manual. Refreshed by the fx-strength-desk-daily task, step 2c.

Real yield direction.note: 10y TIPS ~2.35% on 2026-08-30, down from 2.43% over the prior 30 days - direction is easing, which helps gold, but the level is still historically restrictive so not a full bull signal.

US dollar direction.note: DXY ~99.6, below a declining 200-day MA and testing channel support; bank consensus leans to a modestly weaker dollar into year-end (mid-90s) on slowing US growth and the Warsh rate path. A soft dollar is bullish gold.

Central-bank & ETF demand.note: Central banks bought 6.4x more gold than ETF investors sold in Q2 2026; WGC survey shows the strongest stated buying intention since 2019; ECB says gold has passed US Treasuries as the largest reserve asset (27% of holdings). Western ETF outflows are the one offset, so 4 not higher.

Safe-haven bid.note: US-Israel-Iran conflict in an uneasy pause with Strait of Hormuz risk still live (a ~$4/bbl war premium sits in oil); elevated geopolitical uncertainty keeps a safe-haven bid under gold.

Real yield direction.note: Same falling-real-yield backdrop as gold (10y TIPS 2.43% -> 2.35% over 30 days); silver is more leveraged to the move.

US dollar direction.note: Soft DXY (~99.6, below the 200-day MA, consensus lower into year-end) is bullish silver.

Industrial demand.note: Structural solar/electronics demand stays firm, but 2026 global growth is slowing (IEA has oil demand contracting on trade disruption), which caps the industrial pull. Net mildly positive.

Gold-silver ratio.note: Ratio ~66.8, well below the long-run ~80 average - silver has already closed most of the gap to gold, so it is no longer cheap on this measure. Neutral for further silver outperformance.

OPEC+ supply policy.note: OPEC+ approved a small +188k bpd September hike (2 Aug), completing the rollback of the 2023 voluntary cuts, then signalled quotas held steady through year-end. Removing the 'more barrels coming' overhang is mildly supportive versus the prior path, though all the cut barrels are now back in the market. Next review 6 Sep.

Inventory trend.note: EIA reported a 17.4Mb crude build for the week of 7 Aug (largest since Jan 2023, import-driven), then broadly flat; stocks ~428.9Mb, matching the 5-year average. Level is neutral but the month's trajectory was builds, not draws.

Demand outlook.note: IEA sees 2026 oil demand contracting (~-80 kb/d), with the sharpest quarterly drop since Covid, as trade disruption hits advanced economies, Asia and the Middle East. Clearly bearish.

Geopolitical risk premium.note: Only a modest ~$4/bbl war premium is priced; Hormuz/Iran risk is unresolved and asymmetric to the upside on any escalation. A mild net support.
